objective: Define the canonical logical environment, network trust-zone, deployment-boundary and disaster-recovery topology for NEXUS QUANT without choosing a cloud vendor, geographic region or concrete infrastructure product.
scope: Define logical network trust zones and permitted traffic direction
Define execution enclave and secrets boundary
Define logical backup and disaster-recovery topology
Define recovery classes and critical-state prioritization
Define fail-closed behavior for network/secrets/provider/reconciliation uncertainty
out_of_scope: Select cloud provider, hosting vendor, region, country or datacenter
Select concrete firewall, VPN, KMS, database, queue or observability product
Set final numerical capacity or cost envelopes
Enable Demo, Shadow, Canary, Live or Auto Trading
tests: Every environment has explicit authority and credential boundaries
SHADOW cannot emit live provider commands
CANARY/LIVE are logically isolated from non-production writes
Execution plane cannot be directly reached from public/user ingress
Secrets plane is not directly exposed to agents/UX/data workloads
Observability/audit survives application-plane failure where practical
Cross-environment data movement is directional and governed
DR recovery requires reconciliation before risk-increasing execution
security_tests: Public ingress terminates outside execution/security trust zones
Provider/broker connections are outbound from controlled integration boundaries
No inbound provider callback can directly mutate execution authority without validation
Secrets access is least privilege and environment-bound
Backups remain encrypted/access-controlled in later implementation
Recovery cannot silently broaden network/credential/risk authority
evidence: Logical topology document and machine-readable topology
rollback: Revert P02-G architecture artifacts and state/catalog changes. No infrastructure, region, account or credential is provisioned.
definition_of_done: Task Catalog and Current State are reconciled
